title: afbws schema-first common $defs (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Shared building blocks for the schema-first afbws channels introduced alongside `deal`/`connector`/`bfs`/`account` (see afbws/README convention in CLAUDE.md): a request/response correlation id and a typed error vocabulary. Unlike the legacy afbws channels (discriminated by a `type` const), schema-first channels are routed by `channel` then by a mandatory top-level `schema` id — no `type` field.

requestId.description: Client-generated correlation id (e.g. uuid4), echoed verbatim in the matching response.

instrumentKey.description: Full composite key identifying one catalog listing or derivative: `<MIC>[:<board|market>]:<ticker>` (e.g. `MISX:TQBR:SBER`, `MISX:RFUD:IMOEXF`), or the venueless 2-segment derivative form `<MIC>:<code>` (e.g. `MISX:IMOEXF`) where the wire explicitly identifies a derivative rather than a listing. Case-sensitive, never normalized (`.lower()`/`.upper()`) on either side of the AFB backend<->frontend channel.

accessTier.description: Tier name (axis 1 of the access model): who the user is. An open set defined by DATA (rows of the backend's `tiers` table: e.g. `manager`, `user`, `guest`, a new paid tier `lite`), NOT an enum: a new tier needs no protocol change. Only `manager` is reserved by code (staff, manager functions gated on `tier == manager` independently of `mode`). Comes from the backend's access database (personal `user_roles` and provider-group `group_roles`); the tier with the minimal rank is the default for users not matched by any of them.

accessMode.description: What is available right now (axis 3 of the access model): `full` — paid features work; `basic` — paid features are refused with afbws.access.denied.v1 and the user's alarms/trade plans are held (not evaluated). ALL access logic is decided by `mode` alone.

accessLimits.description: Effective per-user limits (enforced only when ADDING objects; existing objects above a limit are never deleted or truncated). Keys mirror AFB backend/users/roles_loader.py LIMIT_KEYS.

access.title: Effective access of one connection (afbws.auth.v1 response/push `access`).
access.description: Three independent axes. (1) `tier` — WHO the user is (a tier name, open set defined by data; manager functions are gated on `tier == manager` only). (2) `capabilities` — personal permissions granted by a manager, orthogonal to tier (`trade` — real trading through BF, `virtual`, `screener`, `local`); holding `trade` ALWAYS yields `mode: full`: real trading is never held because of a window, a trial or an ended subscription. (3) `mode` — WHAT is available NOW (`full`/`basic`); all logic is decided only by `mode`. When the block changes the server pushes afbws.auth.v1 (no `request_id`) with the whole new block.

capabilities.description: Personal capability names (`trade`, `virtual`, `screener`, `local`; the set is defined by the backend code).
